author: Constitution State News
title: Uzbekistan national charged in federal cargo theft case involving $12 million in goods
text:
Uzbekistan national charged in federal cargo theft case involving $12 million in goods
A citizen of Uzbekistan has been indicted in Connecticut on charges related to a multi-state trucking cargo theft scheme valued at over $12 million in goods. Authorities allege Nursulton Izzatulloevich Khaydarov led efforts using fraudulent company identities before being arrested earlier this year.
Nursulton Izzatulloevich Khaydarov, a 33-year-old citizen of Uzbekistan, was charged by indictment for his alleged involvement in the theft of multiple trucking cargo shipments, according to an Oct. 21 announcement from the U.S. Attorney for the District of Connecticut and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
Court documents allege that since September 2025, Khaydarov and others purchased or assumed control of several motor carrier companies, including their Department of Transportation numbers and business credentials. The group then posed as legitimate business owners to secure contracts for interstate shipments. After picking up shipments from distribution locations, drivers did not deliver them to their intended destinations; instead, the loads were reported stolen. In some cases, co-conspirators made ransom demands for returning stolen goods.
Khaydarov is alleged to have held a valid New Jersey commercial driver’s license as well as fraudulent licenses under various names with altered facial features but his own photograph. Authorities say at least 24 cargo loads containing electronics, clothing, food items, nicotine products and other goods were stolen through this scheme. The estimated retail value of products tied directly to Khaydarov exceeds $12 million.
He was arrested on June 1 in Ontario, California following a federal criminal complaint and indicted by a grand jury on Sept. 22 on conspiracy charges carrying up to five years imprisonment if convicted. Khaydarov pleaded not guilty during his appearance in Bridgeport federal court and has remained detained since his arrest.
U.S. Attorney David X. Sullivan said, “An indictment is not evidence of guilt. Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.”
The ongoing investigation involves several agencies including the FBI; U.S. Department of Transportation – Office of Inspector General; Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation; Homeland Security Investigations; Fullerton Police Department; Ontario Police Department; among others.
This prosecution falls under the Homeland Security Task Force initiative established by Executive Order 14159, which focuses on eliminating criminal cartels and transnational organizations operating within or against U.S. interests—especially those involved with child trafficking or violent crimes committed by foreign nationals.
Anyone with information relevant to this case is encouraged to contact the FBI New Haven Field Office at (203) 777-6311.
The U.S. Attorney for the District of Connecticut serves all residents statewide by prosecuting federal crimes and handling civil matters for the government while employing about 68 assistant attorneys along with support staff members under its parent agency—the Department of Justice—according to the official website.
